record.paper_title: Neutrino production mechanisms in strongly magnetized quark matter: Current status and open questions
record.context_brief: Diquark pairing effects on neutrino emission
record.original_question: When dense quark matter at sufficiently high density forms Cooper pairs and enters a color-superconducting state, how does the specific diquark pairing pattern modify neutrino emission rates and the associated momentum asymmetries in strongly magnetized quark matter? The problem includes determining how different pairing structures, including partially gapped and fully gapped phases, change the neutrino-emission channels relative to unpaired quark matter.

evidence.quote: Second, since quark matter is expected to form Cooper pairs and enter a color-superconducting state at sufficiently high densities [31,49], it is important to investigate the impact of diquark pairing on neutrino emission and the associated momentum asymmetries. Without detailed calculations, one can argue that the results should depend sensitively on the underlying diquark pairing pattern [40].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider dense quark matter at zero temperature and sufficiently high baryon density that quarks near their Fermi surfaces form Cooper pairs (diquark condensates), placing the system in a color-superconducting phase. Suppose, in addition, that the matter is subject to a strong, uniform external magnetic field B (with eB comparable to relevant QCD scales), so that charged quark states are organized into Landau levels and parity along the magnetic-field direction is broken in the weak-interaction sector.

For each of the following diquark pairing patterns, considered separately:
  (i) the unpaired (normal) phase, used as a reference;
  (ii) the 2SC phase, in which only u and d quarks of two colors pair, leaving one color and the s quark ungapped (a partially gapped phase);
  (iii) the color–flavor-locked (CFL) phase, in which u, d, s quarks of all three colors are fully gapped;
  (iv) other partially gapped variants such as the gapless 2SC/CFL or dCFL phases,

compute the differential and total emissivities of the standard neutrino-producing weak processes (direct Urca q1 → q2 + ℓ + ν̄, and modified Urca with a spectator quark) for quark flavors q1, q2 ∈ {u, d, s} and ℓ ∈ {e, μ}, in the presence of the magnetic field B.

In particular:
  (a) Determine the neutrino emissivity ε_ν(T, μ, B) and its parametric dependence on the temperature T, quark chemical potentials, gap parameter Δ, and magnetic field strength B for each pairing pattern listed above, including the suppression factors associated with gapped modes.
  (b) Compute the momentum asymmetry of the emitted neutrinos along the direction of B,
     A := (∫ d³k_ν k_ν,∥ dε_ν/d³k_ν) / (∫ d³k_ν |k_ν| dε_ν/d³k_ν),
  for each pairing pattern, and compare it to the asymmetry obtained in the unpaired phase.
  (c) Identify which neutrino-emission channels remain active, are exponentially suppressed, or are newly opened (e.g., via Cooper-pair-breaking and formation processes) in each pairing pattern, and quantify how A and ε_ν depend qualitatively and quantitatively on the chosen pattern.

The problem is to provide these calculations and a complete characterization of how the diquark pairing pattern modifies neutrino emission rates and associated momentum asymmetries in strongly magnetized quark matter.
artifact.status_search_result: Neutrino emissivity calculations for color-superconducting quark matter (2SC, CFL, gapless variants) exist in zero or weak magnetic fields, but a systematic computation including strong magnetic-field-induced Landau-level structure and momentum asymmetries across the various pairing patterns has not been carried out. The question is identified as an open direction, and no comprehensive solution is found in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Neutrino emissivity in the CFL phase
status_evidence.snippet: Neutrino emission rates from Cooper-pair-breaking and from Goldstone-boson processes have been computed in the CFL phase at B=0.
status_evidence.claim: Emissivities in CFL at zero magnetic field are known, but strong-B extensions with asymmetries are not.

status_evidence.title: Neutrino emission from 2SC quark matter
status_evidence.snippet: Direct Urca processes in 2SC matter are only partially suppressed since one color of u,d remains ungapped.
status_evidence.claim: Pairing pattern qualitatively changes which Urca channels survive, but magnetized-case asymmetries are not computed.
